Let \(a=-x,\ b=-y,\ c=-z\). Since each of \(x,y,z\) is nonpositive, we have \(a,b,c\ge 0\), and the system becomes
\[
a=b^2+c^4,\qquad b=c^2+a^4,\qquad c=a^2+b^4.
\]
If one of \(a,b,c\) is \(0\), then all are \(0\). Otherwise assume \(a,b,c>0\).

Let \(s>0\) be the unique root of \(s^3+s-1=0\). One can show any positive solution must have \(a=b=c=s\): cyclically rotate so \(a\) is the maximum, then split into \(b\ge c\) or \(c\ge b\). In either case, inequalities force \(a=b=c\). Then
\[
t=t^2+t^4 \implies t(t^3+t-1)=0,
\]
so the positive solution is \(t=s\).

Thus the only real solutions are
\[
(x,y,z)=(0,0,0)\quad\text{or}\quad (x,y,z)=(-s,-s,-s).
\]
For \((-s,-s,-s)\),
\[
x^3+y^3+z^3=-3s^3=-3(1-s).
\]
Since \(s^3+s=1\) and \(s>2/3\), we have \(0<3s^3<1\), so
\[
-1< -3s^3<0.
\]
Therefore
\[
\left\lfloor x^3+y^3+z^3\right\rfloor=-1
\]
at the nonzero solution, while it is \(0\) at the origin. Hence \(m=-1\).

The modulo \(2007\) residue of \(-1\) is
\[
\boxed{2006}.
\]
